text: Sweden participated in the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, Australia, with the exception of the equestrian events, which were held five months earlier in Stockholm, Sweden due to quarantine regulations. A total of 97 competitors—83 men and 14 women—took part in 74 events across 14 sports in Australia and 6 events in one sport in Sweden. Swedish athletes earned 19 medals, including 3 gold medals from the equestrian events held in Stockholm. The men's events included the Marathon, Team Time Trial, and Individual Road Race, while the equestrian disciplines were Dressage, Eventing, and Jumping. Five male fencers represented Sweden, three male pentathletes competed, and Lars Hall won gold in the individual pentathlon. Nine male rowers participated in two of the seven rowing events. Eight shooters competed, with Olof Sköldberg winning silver in the 100m running deer and John Sundberg winning bronze in the 50 m rifle, three positions.
